Subject: Post-call: SLO drill — p95/p99 hosted vs incumbent (benchmark window & asks)

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can lock the benchmark window and test harness details.

What we heard from NebulaCare (confirm if anything below needs correcting):
- Primary endpoint: inference for clinical summarization (avg token length ~120).
- Traffic envelope: steady-state ~40 req/s, short bursts up to 120 req/s (90s windows).
- Tail sensitivity: p95 target ~120ms end-to-end, p99 target ~300ms (including network + client serialization).
- Streaming: client opens streaming sessions for long responses; we should test 8 concurrent streams per instance with ~1s token bursts.
- Concurrency: observed 250 concurrent clients at peak across their fleet; for our hosted probe they want a scaled window representative of 10% of peak.

Asks from Redwood to prepare an apples-to-apples hosted vs incumbent benchmark:
1) Provide sample payloads and representative request mix (percent short/medium/long). Please attach JSON payloads and a sample JWT for test account.
2) Confirm whether NebulaCare can allow an IP whitelist or temporary test creds for the benchmark window.
3) Agree on benchmark window (proposed windows below).
4) If there are special network paths (VPN, proxy) that add latency, flag them up front.

Our proposed test config (draft):
- Traffic generator: 3-minute steady blocks with 2x 90s burst windows every 15 minutes.
- Measurement: end-to-end p95/p99 measured at client side; include server traces (we'll capture traces you share).
- Warmup: 20 minutes with representative traffic to populate KV cache.
- Fallbacks: run hosted baseline (quantized medium), then full-precision baseline, then incumbent run.

Proposed benchmark slot: 2027-07-06 13:00-16:00 PT. If that doesn't work, give 2 alternative slots.

Attachments: slo-test-plan.csv (test matrix), trace-sample-20270626.json (example trace we want).

Next steps / owners:
- Anne: confirm sample payloads + test creds (owner: NebulaCare)
- David: provide brief doc on their edge/proxy topology (owner: NebulaCare)
- Ben: draft exact traffic generator script and share in-drive (owner: Ben Carter)
- Camila: schedule benchmark and invite infra (owner: Camila Reyes)

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan — quick internal notes / proposed test knobs before we lock the window.

High-level: we can reproduce the envelope but we need to be explicit about CDN/edge hops. If NebulaCare's proxy adds 30-50ms, that shifts p95 baseline. Ask them to provide a traceroute + single-sample tcp ping.

Test knobs I recommend we exercise:
- Streaming concurrency: run 8, 16 streams to show slope; streaming tail is often where p99 diverges.
- Batch sizes: run with batch=1, batch=8 to show cost/latency tradeoff.
- KV cache hit vs cold: run warmup vs cold-start to quantify delta.
- Fallback policy: ensure we test a quantized variant for cost comparisons but measure quality separately.

Operational notes for the run:
- Canary: start hosted run at 10% of target load, validate tails for 5m, then ramp — reduces noise from warmups.
- Trace capture: we'll ask NebulaCare to include an X-Trace-Id header so we can stitch traces client<->server.

I'll draft the traffic generator (Gatling script) and upload to the drive by EOD Monday. Camila — can you tentatively hold 07/06 and 07/07 for infra?

Ben
